summary: Postinstall native dropper decrypts and executes staged payload with CI/sandbox evasion
details: The package ships only prebuilt native addons (`prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/node.napi.node`) plus an opaque 2.4 MB sidecar `.napi_cache`, with no build system, no source, no README, and an empty `module.exports={}` main — the advertised 'Cache helper utilities' purpose has no implementation. `package.json` declares `postinstall: node _setup.js`, and both `_setup.js` and `index.js` load the platform-specific native addon. On Linux the addon reads `%s/.napi_cache`, writes it to `/tmp/.<pid>`, and executes it via `fork` + `setsid` + `execlp` (daemonization). On Windows it writes `%TEMP%\<name>.nc<pid>.js`, sets hidden file attributes via `SetFileAttributesA`, and launches it via `CreateProcessA` as `node "%s"`. Before executing, the addon gates on anti-analysis checks: environment variables `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITLAB_CI`, `CIRCLECI`, `JENKINS_URL`, `BUILDKITE`, `CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID`, `APPVEYOR`, `SEMAPHORE`, `TEAMCITY_VERSION`, `SANDBOX`; container markers `/proc/1/cgroup`, `kubepod`, `containerd`, `dockerinit`; debugger checks `TracerPid`, `/proc/self/maps`, `IsDebuggerPresent`, `CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent`; and Toolhelp32 process enumeration for `wireshark`/`httpdebug`. Installing the package on a developer workstation causes an opaque encrypted payload to be decoded and executed as a detached process on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
